query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Doping MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials with a small amount of boron can improve their mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.conditions: Low boron concentration (<1 at.%) and appropriate heat treatment
generation.mechanism: Boron doping reduces grain size, increases grain boundary area, and enhances mechanical strength without significantly degrading magnetocaloric properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical strength and retained large magnetocaloric effect
generation.boundary: Boron concentration >1 at.% may degrade magnetocaloric properties
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient data on the optimal boron concentration and heat treatment conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare MnNiSi-based materials with varying boron concentrations (0-2 at.%) and measure their mechanical strength and magnetocaloric effect
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the material with 1 at.% boron shows a significant decrease in magnetocaloric effect (>20%) or no improvement in mechanical strength, the hypothesis is falsified
